package.author: Daniel Mevit
package.description: Free, offline voice-to-text dictation. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words appear in any app — 100% local, powered by Whisper.

en-US.author: Daniel Mevit
en-US.description: Free, offline voice-to-text dictation. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words appear in any app — 100% local, powered by Whisper.
en-US.longDescription:
Eqho is an always-on dictation app that lives in your system tray. Press a
global hotkey (default Alt+Q), speak naturally, and the transcribed text is
typed into whatever application is focused. Speech recognition runs entirely
on your machine via OpenAI's Whisper models (faster-whisper and whisper.cpp) —
no cloud, no account, no API keys. Uses NVIDIA graphics cards (CUDA) and AMD/Intel graphics cards (Vulkan);
PCs without one run on the processor. Includes a live transcription overlay, searchable
local history, custom vocabulary, voice commands, and text replacements.
en-US.name: Eqho
en-US.releaseNotes:
The dictation pill moves with your voice — and you can tune it.
- The pill moves like water. While you speak, its lines rise into soft, flowing swells — taller when you're louder, a little livelier with a higher voice — and settle into calm, nearly flat lines when you pause. Eqho still hears and transcribes exactly the same audio.
- Pill and text box settings (Settings → Overlay): pill size (60–140 %), and how see-through the pill and the text box are, each from Solid to Clear. The pill is now 20 % smaller by default; the text box looks as before.
- Dictations stay out of Windows clipboard history. Eqho marks the text it pastes as private, so it doesn't pile up in Win+V or sync to the cloud clipboard — and that removes the last rare case of a dictation typing nothing.
- Calmer spacing in the dashboard: one even gap between cards, a little less than the room at the window edge.
- Choosing a model highlights it right away, and the empty Custom Vocabulary box shows a grey example of what to add.
Full details: CHANGELOG
